context.why: This package is a UI layer for payment backends. Its whole promise is that a project installs it beside a backend, adds one line to its URL configuration, and that backend's pages appear in django-mvp's Account Center with no view, template or menu entry written in the project. This story builds that arrival mechanism and the drf-stripe namespace's three pages. The foundational phase is already done and committed: the backend is installed in the demo, the Account Center and sign-in are mounted there, and the standards document has been amended to allow views beyond template rendering.

prior_decisions: D1 — one Contribution object per namespace; ready(), the URL configuration and the card all read one function for the available ones, so the three surfaces cannot drift apart. Not a base class; nothing subclasses it.

D2 — URL names are grouped under one application namespace, app_name = 'payments', and each name carries its namespace slug, e.g. payments:drf-stripe-subscription. A Django URL namespace named after the backend was rejected because a project can claim that name by mounting the backend's own URLs under it.

D3 — availability has two halves. is_available() asks the application registry only, because ready() and urls.py both call it and neither may reverse a URL. is_reachable() asks whether this namespace's pages reverse, and only a render-time caller may ask. Build both in T010; the card in US-3 uses the second.
D4 — mvp_payments must precede mvp in INSTALLED_APPS for the template override to resolve. The README currently says the opposite and T017 corrects it.
D5 — register() is idempotent by entry name, because ready() runs again on every development-server reload and the menu tree survives it.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given a contribution whose backend application label is installed, when it is asked, then it reports itself available; when the label is not installed, then it does not. Given three declared pages, when url_patterns() is called, then it returns exactly three routes named for the namespace and page; when register() is called, then exactly three navigation entries exist.
Given a contribution already registered, when register() runs a second time, then the rendered Account Center navigation still shows each entry exactly once.

Given the URL configuration is mounted, when each of the three page names is reversed under the payments namespace, then it resolves to a page view; when a name belonging to no declared page is reversed, then it raises NoReverseMatch.

Given a signed-in person, when they request each contributed page, then it renders inside the Account Center layout carrying that page's heading and the Account Center navigation. Given an anonymous visitor, when they request one directly, then they are redirected to the sign-in location.

Given the drf-stripe contribution, when it is inspected, then it names the backend's application label and declares exactly three pages with the expected slugs and translatable labels; and when a signed-in person opens the Account Center, then one navigation entry per page is rendered.
